title: [Medium][NAV-014] Streaming sample cancellation does not interrupt its synchronous read loop
body:
<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:NAV-014 -->
## Classification
- **Finding:** NAV-014
- **Priority:** Medium
- **Evidence status:** `confirmed-source` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `sample:common`
- **Estimated complexity:** S
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`sample/common/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf.sample/screens/FilePickerScreen.kt:88-103`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/sample/common/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf.sample/screens/FilePickerScreen.kt#L88-L103) — `streamingJob cancellation`
- [`sample/common/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf.sample/screens/FilePickerScreen.kt:313-345`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/sample/common/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf.sample/screens/FilePickerScreen.kt#L313-L345) — `describeStreaming/countBytes`

## Root cause
Replacing a selection cancels the old job, but countBytes loops over synchronous RawSource reads without suspension or checking coroutine cancellation. withContext(Default) and catching/rethrowing CancellationException do not inject a check inside that loop.

## Impact and preconditions
A cancelled or no-longer-visible sample operation can continue consuming CPU/storage until EOF or I/O failure. The surrounding use correctly closes the source on exit; this finding is delayed cancellation, not a confirmed never-close leak.

## Supporting evidence
- All source locations refer to immutable baseline af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6.
- cancel at line93 is not observed inside while(true) lines339-344.
- use at line319 and explicit CancellationException rethrow at321-322 are positive existing cleanup behavior.
- PR545 introduced the demo; its own description notes browsers still load whole files while the KDoc lines313-315 says the file never needs to fit in memory.

## Recommended solution
Make the loop cancellation-cooperative with an explicit coroutine-context check per bounded chunk and test with a deliberately slow source. Document that the browser RawSource path currently buffers the whole Blob before the sample loop; fixed read chunks do not make that platform constant-memory.

## Risks and compatibility
An OS read may itself be uninterruptible; checking before chunks limits delay but is not a hard real-time cancellation guarantee. Browser buffering belongs to the I/O implementation audit.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Slow fake source counts reads after cancellation and proves prompt termination/close.
- Reselect a file and leave the screen while counting; old work stops and does not overwrite new results.
- Run large native/JVM input with a defined cancellation latency bound.
- Correct sample memory claims for JS/Wasm buffering.

## Dependencies
- None identified.

## Historical context
- https://github.com/MohamedRejeb/Calf/pull/545
- https://github.com/MohamedRejeb/Calf/issues/537

- [`sample/common/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf.sample/screens/PermissionsScreen.kt:53-80`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/sample/common/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf.sample/screens/PermissionsScreen.kt#L53-L80) — `PermissionScreen requested permissions`
- [`sample/android/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:9-37`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/sample/android/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml#L9-L37) — `uses-permission declarations`
- [`calf-permissions/core/src/androidMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/permissions/StoragePermissions.android.kt:37-40`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-permissions/core/src/androidMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/permissions/StoragePermissions.android.kt#L37-L40) — `Permission.Call mapping`

## Root cause
The menu requests Permission.Call, mapped to CALL_PHONE, but the sample manifest never declares CALL_PHONE. Conversely it declares MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE and READ/SEND/RECEIVE_SMS without a corresponding special-access workflow/SMS demo in this sample.

## Impact and preconditions
The Call permission example cannot demonstrate a normal grant for the declared app. Broad/unrelated declarations mislead integrators and can impose distribution-policy scrutiny; a declaration alone does not grant access or establish a security vulnerability.

## Supporting evidence
- All source locations refer to immutable baseline af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6.
- Permission.Call is the first menu row at line56; no CALL_PHONE declaration occurs in sample manifest lines9-37.
- StoragePermissions.android.kt maps Permission.Call to Manifest.permission.CALL_PHONE.
- MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE is declared at14-15 and SMS at35-37. iOS calendar/Bonjour mismatches are assigned to the separate permissions audit.
- Cross-review boundary: PERM-024 owns the broad-storage documentation/WriteStorage special-access mismatch. NAV-015 primarily fixes Call/menu/manifest consistency; unrelated broad declarations are context, not a duplicate all-files-access issue.

## Recommended solution
Align explicit demonstration scenarios and merged manifests; remove unrelated permissions or split narrowly scoped demo variants. Teach special-access APIs separately from ordinary runtime permissions. Keep Android SDK/version constraints and iOS usage keys in the permission module's test matrix.

## Risks and compatibility
Do not add sensitive permissions to a general sample merely to make all status rows turn green. FileProvider is nonexported and uses grantUriPermissions; its cache path is not evidence of universally exposed storage.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Inspect the merged manifest and map every menu permission to its expected declaration/status for supported API levels.
- Test Call on a fresh installation under an explicitly approved demo variant.
- Verify file/image picker operation without MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE and unrelated SMS permissions.
- Run permission denial/permanent-denial and Android13/14 media-selection scenarios.

title: [Medium][PERM-001] Android silently treats an unregistered Permission as granted
body:
<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:PERM-001 -->
## Classification
- **Finding:** PERM-001
- **Priority:** Medium
- **Evidence status:** `confirmed-source` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-permissions/core`
- **Estimated complexity:** M
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-permissions/core/src/androidMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/permissions/PermissionsUtil.android.kt:101-111`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-permissions/core/src/androidMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/permissions/PermissionsUtil.android.kt#L101-L111) — `toAndroidPermission/isAlwaysGranted`
- [`calf-permissions/core/src/androidMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/permissions/MutablePermissionState.android.kt:86-99,118-126`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-permissions/core/src/androidMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/permissions/MutablePermissionState.android.kt#L86-L99) — `launchPermissionRequest/getPermissionStatus`
- [`calf-permissions/core/src/androidMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/permissions/AndroidPermissionRegistry.kt:24-38`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-permissions/core/src/androidMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/permissions/AndroidPermissionRegistry.kt#L24-L38) — `register/getMapping/findByAndroidString`

## Root cause
No mapping and a deliberately out-of-SDK-range mapping both become the empty string. The state interprets either as Granted and calls onPermissionResult(true). The public open Permission class permits custom permissions without an Android registration.

## Impact and preconditions
Missing custom integration is indistinguishable from real authorization and differs from the explicit missing-delegate error on iOS. Consumers may attempt protected operations and fail at the OS boundary. This is not an OS permission bypass.

## Supporting evidence
- Exact toAndroidPermission logic returned empty for Permission("Unregistered") in the isolated JVM harness. Source then returns Granted for empty.
- iOS PermissionDelegateRegistry.getDelegate throws for missing registration.
- Upstream #191 explicitly confirms RemoteNotification was intentionally iOS-specific.

## Recommended solution
Distinguish Registered, NotApplicable, and Unknown mapping results; fail clearly for Unknown, preserve explicitly documented no-op permissions, and validate custom names/ranges. Define main-thread registration or synchronize/freeze the registry.

## Risks and compatibility
Existing callers may rely on custom unknown permissions being no-ops. RemoteNotification on Android is intentionally iOS-only and documented as Granted; do not silently redefine that compatibility contract as part of this fix. Concurrent registry mutation is a risk, not an observed exploit.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Custom unknown permission on Android/iOS gives a consistent diagnostic.
- Out-of-range mappings remain explicit not-applicable, including Notification below33.
- Custom registration/name collision and concurrent registration/lookup tests.

## Dependencies
- None identified.

## Historical context
- https://github.com/MohamedRejeb/Calf/issues/191
- https://github.com/MohamedRejeb/Calf/commit/7d382c69ba93e218a210239ed9dfc99a34660be0

title: [Medium][PERM-003] Android bulk/child permission requests do not consistently deliver completion callbacks
body:
<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:PERM-003 -->
## Classification
- **Finding:** PERM-003
- **Priority:** Medium
- **Evidence status:** `confirmed-source` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-permissions/core`
- **Estimated complexity:** M
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-permissions/core/src/androidMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/permissions/MutableMultiplePermissionsState.android.kt:70-95,130-140`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-permissions/core/src/androidMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/permissions/MutableMultiplePermissionsState.android.kt#L70-L95) — `rememberMutablePermissionsState/launchMultiplePermissionRequest`

## Root cause
The empty-string safeguard returns without invoking onPermissionsResult when all permissions are filtered; mixed batches omit not-applicable keys. A child state within a multiple state has a RequestPermission callback that only refreshes status and never invokes the supplied parent result callback; its always-granted fast path does invoke it.

## Impact and preconditions
Callback-driven workflows can wait forever for a batch containing only out-of-range permissions, and child request behavior varies by native applicability. This survives the historical crash fix.

## Supporting evidence
- The only callback in bulk path is inside ActivityResult launcher; line136 guards launcher execution with no else.
- Child launcher lines85-89 refresh state but do not invoke its onPermissionResult.

## Recommended solution
Define and implement one completion contract: return a complete logical result map even for empty/not-applicable batches; route child launcher results to the current child/parent callback; document whether an empty input completes with an empty map.

## Risks and compatibility
Do not remove the filter added for Android10: passing empty permission strings was an actual historical crash. Callback normalization can reveal code relying on silence.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Empty input, all-inapplicable input, mixed real/inapplicable input on API29/33.
- Launch a child state with a runtime permission and an always-granted permission; assert exactly one callback.
- Lifecycle disposal/recreation must not deliver duplicate callbacks.

## Dependencies

## Historical context

body:
<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:PERM-005 -->
## Classification
- **Finding:** PERM-005
- **Priority:** Medium
- **Evidence status:** `confirmed-source` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-permissions/core`
- **Estimated complexity:** S
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-permissions/core/src/iosMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/permissions/MutablePermissionState.ios.kt:39-45,63-81`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-permissions/core/src/iosMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/permissions/MutablePermissionState.ios.kt#L39-L45) — `rememberMutablePermissionState/MutablePermissionStateImpl`
- [`calf-permissions/core/src/iosMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/permissions/MutableMultiplePermissionsState.ios.kt:45-53`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-permissions/core/src/iosMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/permissions/MutableMultiplePermissionsState.ios.kt#L45-L53) — `rememberMutablePermissionsState`
- [`calf-permissions/core/src/androidMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/permissions/MutablePermissionState.android.kt:39-45,79-94`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-permissions/core/src/androidMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/permissions/MutablePermissionState.android.kt#L39-L45) — `rememberMutablePermissionState/fast path`
- [`calf-permissions/core/src/androidMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/permissions/MutableMultiplePermissionsState.android.kt:70-78`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-permissions/core/src/androidMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/permissions/MutableMultiplePermissionsState.android.kt#L70-L78) — `rememberMutablePermissionsState`

## Root cause
Objects remembered only by permission/list capture onPermissionResult in a constructor val. Later recompositions with a new callback do not update it. Android ActivityResult callbacks use the recomposed lambda, but the direct always-granted path uses the old constructor callback; iOS uses it for every result.

## Impact and preconditions
A permission result can invoke stale navigation, state, or business logic after recomposition. Android behavior differs for runtime vs not-applicable permissions.

## Supporting evidence
- The remembered objects have immutable private callback fields, and remember keys omit callback identity.

## Recommended solution
Use rememberUpdatedState for callback delegation or update an internal callback holder every composition without recreating native helper state. Include context/lifecycle ownership in remembrance decisions.

## Risks and compatibility
Recreating the permission helper on every callback change would introduce native request churn and lose in-flight callbacks; preserve request identity while updating the callback reference.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Recompose callback A to B, request same permission, assert only B is called.
- Repeat for iOS, Android runtime and empty-mapping fast paths, and child states within a batch.

## Dependencies
- None identified.

Every delegate status except accepted authorization is treated as final false, including NotDetermined. The enclosing delegate closure clears the single pending callback after invoking it. A new request overwrites the previous callback, and a reentrant callback can install a new one that is then cleared by the old completion.

## Impact and preconditions
An initial/in-progress authorization event arriving while a request is pending completes it as denied and drops the later grant; rapid/reentrant requests lose results. Apple schedules initial authorization callbacks when a manager initializes, making event ordering important.

Ignore nonterminal status events, correlate callbacks to request generation, clear/take the old callback before invocation, coalesce or reject overlap explicitly, and cancel pending work at owner disposal.

## Risks and compatibility
The adapter test deliberately injects NotDetermined after launch; frequency and timing on actual iOS devices are not established. Permission UI cannot be reliably cancelled, so disposal should suppress delivery without claiming OS revocation.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Initial NotDetermined followed by grant/deny produces one terminal result.
- Double tap, reentrant launch in callback, status event after disposal, multiple helper instances.

Strongly retain a per-request delegate/context, serialize requests, clear by identity before notifying, stop scan in finally, and provide disposal/timeout as explicit non-denial outcomes. Only scan in a powered-on state.

The historical PR reports device tests passing common flows; preserve those fixes. Kotlin/Native GC/ObjC lifetime behavior must be measured before claiming the weak delegate is the actual cause of a production failure.

## Root cause
Two status variants collapse not-determined, restricted, permanently denied, limited and unsupported states. Fine/Coarse share a location helper that never checks accuracyAuthorization; contacts limited falls into denial; Photos uses legacy APIs that may report limited access as Authorized; provisional notifications count as Granted without delivery capability detail.

## Impact and preconditions
A granted FineLocation does not prove precise location on iOS, a limited contacts grant is unusable through the abstraction, and callers cannot distinguish partial gallery access or provisional alerts. - Historical #154/#229/#258/#284 show repeated confusion around the Boolean rationale convention.

## Recommended solution
Add a capability/result model alongside the compatibility Boolean API: requestability/denial reason, limited scope, iOS accuracy level and notification delivery modes. Use modern access-level APIs with availability guards. Document old Granted as a coarse permission signal, never full resource access.

## Risks and compatibility
A new sealed variant can break exhaustive when expressions; prefer additive API or a deliberate major migration. Photos limited behavior differs between legacy and modern query APIs, so do not assert legacy query currently denies every limited grant.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- iOS reduced/full accuracy and temporary full accuracy, limited/full contacts, selected/all photos, provisional/ephemeral notifications.
- Android14 selected media, approximate location, first deny/second deny/never asked and unsupported targets.

## Dependencies
- None identified.

## Root cause
Every bind replaces a shared client and adds an observer to the supplied lifecycle without removing previous observers. Old observers dereference the current client on destruction. isStarted survives destruction; scope/channels are never cancelled/closed and callbacks do not check active generation.

## Impact and preconditions
Destroying an old lifecycle after rebinding can stop/null the new client. Repeated binds and in-flight callbacks can retain tracker/owner references or deliver after stop; scope work has no explicit shutdown contract.

- Observer at lines49-54 captures the tracker and uses mutable locationProviderClient, not the client/owner it was created for.

## Recommended solution
Have one bound-owner token/observer/client at a time, detach/remove old updates on rebind, use a cancellable lifecycle-owned scope, clear active state on destruction and reject late callbacks by generation. Remove unused fragmentManager argument through a compatibility deprecation.

## Risks and compatibility
Source proves cross-owner interference; actual leak duration depends on FusedLocation callbacks and Android lifecycle GC. Do not close reusable channels without defining restart semantics.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Bind A,start,bind B,destroy A: B continues; destroy B stops exactly once.
- Repeated bind/start/stop, queued callback after stop, destruction/restart, weak-reference/leak checks.

- intersect chooses max(min) and min(max) with no empty-state check.
- CalendarViewHost constructs NSDateInterval(startDate=start,endDate=end) without comparing endpoints.

## Recommended solution
Represent/recognize empty effective bounds explicitly. Disable selection with safe native bounds or expose a documented validation error; handle direct reversed bounds and disjoint and-compositions consistently. Do not prohibit useful empty intersections without an API policy.

## Risks and compatibility
Pure rule evaluation currently correctly rejects every date for a disjoint interval. A fix must preserve that semantics and not accidentally expand an empty range to all dates.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Direct reversed min/max; same UTC day with reversed intraday endpoints; disjoint and rules.

<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:UI-037 -->
## Classification
- **Finding:** UI-037
- **Priority:** Medium
- **Evidence status:** `risk` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-ui`
- **Estimated complexity:** M
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-ui/src/iosMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/ui/utils/ImageUtils.kt:71-100`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-ui/src/iosMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/ui/utils/ImageUtils.kt#L71-L100) — `ImageBitmap.toUIImage`

## Root cause
PixelMap Color.toArgb values are copied to UIntArray and handed as raw bytes to a context configured as kCGImageAlphaPremultipliedLast without an explicit matching byte-order/premultiplication conversion. data.refTo(0) is scoped to the create call even though the context uses external pixel storage until snapshotting.

## Impact and preconditions
Little-endian ARGB words occupy B,G,R,A bytes, so the requested CoreGraphics interpretation may swap channels and blend translucent pixels incorrectly. Pointer-lifetime assumptions deserve a pinned ownership check; actual use-after-free is not established.

## Supporting evidence
- All cited source locations refer to immutable upstream baseline af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6.
- data is pixelMap.buffer.toUIntArray() and bitmapInfo is kCGImageAlphaPremultipliedLast.
- The buffer address is supplied via data.refTo(0), with no enclosing usePinned region.

## Recommended solution
Specify one exact pixel format, explicitly convert/premultiply as needed, use matching CoreGraphics flags, and keep the buffer pinned for context creation through snapshot/release. Validate the result rather than assuming flag names match Kotlin integer layout.

## Risks and compatibility
This is a portability/native-interop risk, not a confirmed memory-safety vulnerability. Kotlin/Native GC behavior and CoreGraphics byte-order semantics must be verified on the real target.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Known1x1 red/blue/green/transparent/half-alpha pixels roundtrip to UIImage and composite over black/white.

## Root cause
Every external value update starts animation jobs and every animated value callback starts another velocity animation. Release jobs delay/wait and are not cancelled on the next press. Fast updates/re-presses can accumulate work and let an old release reset a new press. Wall-clock adjustments can distort velocity. Persistent memory leakage or visible jank has not been measured.

Use structured, single-owner jobs for value/velocity/press state, cancel obsolete release jobs on new interaction and synchronize all mutation paths. Use monotonic pointer/frame timestamps and profile coroutine/allocation counts before optimizing constants.

## Risks and compatibility
Compose Animatable already cancels conflicting animations, which limits some overlap; that does not automatically cancel all sibling/external jobs. Avoid asserting an unbounded leak without measurements.

<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:IO-016 -->
## Classification

- **Priority:** Low
- **Evidence status:** `confirmed-test` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)

- **Estimated complexity:** S

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-file-picker/src/desktopMain/kotlin/jodd/net/MimeTypes.kt:104-105,123-124,133-159`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-file-picker/src/desktopMain/kotlin/jodd/net/MimeTypes.kt#L104-L105) — `MIME registration/lookup/search`

## Root cause
MIME/extension normalization uses Locale.getDefault instead of protocol-stable ROOT. Multi-MIME parsing splits only the exact string comma-space. Each map entry recomputes lowercase, creates a vararg array and runs an unused findAnyOf; wildcard matching recursively backtracks without a complexity bound.

## Impact and preconditions
Under Turkish locale uppercase TIFF/MIME I letters can miss mappings; comma-separated MIME lists without spaces return no results. All searches scan the full map and allocate unnecessarily. Pathological caller-supplied wildcard patterns can consume disproportionate CPU; no remote attack surface was demonstrated.

## Supporting evidence
- Kotlin harness confirms lookupMimeType(TIFF) is null under tr-TR while lowercase tiff resolves, and image/jpeg,image/png yields no extensions but comma-space yields four.
- Lines 143 and 146 show unused work and per-entry vararg conversion; no performance benchmark was used to claim a regression.

## Recommended solution
Normalize with Locale.ROOT, split on comma and trim/filter empties, precompute pattern arrays/reverse MIME index, remove the unused search, and replace or bound general recursive wildcard matching. Either remove unused mutable registration or synchronize/copy-on-write if used concurrently.

## Risks and compatibility
These helpers are internal; optimize demonstrated common filters first. Do not claim a security vulnerability from internal worst-case matching alone. Case-sensitive extensions on native dialogs need a deliberate policy.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- tr-TR uppercase TIFF and IMAGE/PNG
- Comma lists with zero/multiple spaces
- Known scalar/wildcard equivalence
- Adversarial bounded wildcard performance
- Concurrent registration only if that API is retained

## Root cause
When user.home is absent the fixed .cache/calf-filepicker directory is placed under java.io.tmpdir, potentially shared with other users. mkdirs and reads follow existing filesystem entries without ownership/symlink validation, and verification/load are separated. System.loadLibrary is intentionally tried first without an ABI/content check.

## Impact and preconditions
In nondefault deployments with attacker-writable cache/search-path components, a local attacker may race or substitute executable native code. Normal private-home usage reduces the threat substantially; truncated SHA-256 naming is cache isolation, not an authenticity guarantee. No compromise was reproduced.

## Supporting evidence
- The fallback at loader line 68 selects java.io.tmpdir but appends a fixed directory, not a unique private directory.
- Baseline verifies existing bytes and uses unique temp files/atomic move with fallback; positive cache probes passed.
- System-library-first behavior was deliberately added by 6331db2 for packagers and is not inherently a vulnerability.
- The separate share-cache issue NATIVE-031 uses a constant target name; it is not the same bug as this picker hardening risk. Picker content-addressing is an existing remediation reference for share.

## Recommended solution
Create a private randomized fallback directory with restrictive permissions, validate cache ownership/no-follow policy, document trusted java.library.path deployment requirements, and consider ABI version negotiation for externally packaged libraries. Retain the safe identical-content reuse fix.

## Risks and compatibility
A same-user attacker often already controls the process; do not exaggerate this as remote code execution. OS signing/quarantine and Windows loaded-DLL behavior must remain compatible. Cache names retain upstream identifiers intentionally for binary compatibility.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Missing user.home with shared temp directory
- Precreated symlink/foreign-owned cache directory
- Concurrent extraction and failed move
- Mismatched native ABI from system path

## Root cause
Every setter invokes a full native settings reapply even when assigning the same value; Desktop queues one FX task per setter and each task reads the whole live settings object. Android records each resource error by copying the entire accumulated list with toList().

## Impact and preconditions
Configuration batches cause redundant native/JNI/FX work; many failed resources allocate quadratically many error-list elements over a request. No benchmark demonstrates a user-visible slowdown yet, so this is an optimization candidate rather than a release-blocking defect.

Skip equal-value notifications, batch/transaction settings changes or apply field deltas on the correct UI thread, and choose a bounded/batched immutable error reporting strategy that preserves diagnostics. Measure before and after.

## Risks and compatibility
Coalescing updates may alter observable timing; mutable collections must not leak through supposedly immutable UI state. Bounded diagnostics need an explicit truncation/count indicator rather than silently discarding errors.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Assign identical settings repeatedly and apply a multi-setting batch; assert bounded native/FX calls.
- Thousands of resource failures: benchmark allocation/time and preserve required error metadata.

title: [Medium][Migration] Unpublish unintended legacy Pages deployment without deleting preserved history
body:
<!-- nativeCmpkit-operational:pages-unpublish-20261024 -->
## Classification

**Medium priority — confirmed migration/hosting control incident, not an additional baseline library defect.** Existing deployment unpublishing requires the repository owner's GitHub UI action. Legacy branch publishing has already been disabled. No releases or packages were published.

## Evidence and affected configuration

- Destination: `Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit`; Pages initially reported `build_type=legacy`, source `gh-pages:/`.
- GitHub deployment **7300258890**, actor `github-pages[bot]`, recorded success at **2026-10-24T14:58:51Z**.
- Source is the preserved historical commit **2c3055c523ed6efe183d828b7a7942d357cd4d29**, not the new nativeCmpkit documentation.
- Three `DELETE /repos/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/pages` requests returned definitive HTTP422: `Deactivating GitHub pages for this repository is not allowed.` This persisted after changing publishing mode to `workflow` and trying the current documented API version.
- [Incident narrative](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/main/docs/migration/pages-incident.md), [structured incident](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/main/docs/migration/pages-incident.json), and linked API/status receipts retain exact IDs, timestamps, responses and ref verification.

## Root cause and impact

The historical publishing branch was selected by legacy Pages hosting; disabling GitHub Actions alone did not establish that Pages was inactive. The exact internal activation mechanism is not proven. GitHub recorded a successful bot deployment during ref import although no migration command requested a deployment.

An old upstream site may be available under the owner's project route, contrary to the migration's no-deployment intent. Public reachability/content and CDN cache expiration were not verified. No secret disclosure or exploit is established.

## Recommended action

1. Open [Settings → Pages](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/settings/pages) and select **Unpublish site** next to the current deployment.
2. **Do not delete, rename or force-push `gh-pages`**: preserving its original ref and history is a migration requirement.
3. Keep `build_type=workflow`; current verification workflows have read-only permissions and no Pages deployment step. Leave Actions disabled outside supervised verification.
4. Append an observed resolution to the incident record, retaining the failed API attempts and original deployment history.

GitHub documents [unpublishing as separate from deleting configuration](https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/unpublishing-a-github-pages-site). The owner has already been asked; no response or completed action is assumed.

## Verification / risks

- Verify the existing deployment is unpublished; distinguish owner confirmation, API state and any independent URL check. Do not infer that `has_pages=true/false` alone proves CDN content expiration.
- Recheck the original `gh-pages` SHA and every preserved non-main branch/tag.
- Confirm no additional deployments or publishing workflows were triggered.
- Preserve all incident receipts; do not rewrite history to conceal the event.

Effort: **S**, administrative; dependency: owner UI access because the public REST deletion route refused the request. This operational follow-up is separate from the 164 baseline findings and 170 managed audit/history issues, avoiding a duplicate or misleading reopening of BUILD-008.
